resolve: https://www.screener.in/company/<OUR-NSE-SYMBOL>/ (standalone) or /consolidated/ for the consolidated variant. Our NSE symbol IS the screener slug for all 3 probes (RELIANCE, MCX, ETERNAL) -- no separate lookup table needed. Old/renamed symbols do NOT redirect: /company/ZOMATO/consolidated/ -> HTTP 404 (confirmed by curl); the site only recognizes the current ticker ETERNAL. So renamed names need the SAME _rename_map.json our own pipeline already uses to pick the current symbol before building the URL. BSE-only names (no NSE symbol) were not probed here but screener's own search/autocomplete (not tested, would need a request) is the likely fallback route -- flag for P2/P4. Bulk-resolvable: YES for any stock with a live NSE symbol (URL is a pure template, zero per-stock discovery cost); each page also embeds a numeric internal 'data-company-id' (RELIANCE=2726, MCX=2156, ETERNAL=1274894) used only for the site's own AJAX calls, not needed for resolution.
category_notes: Screener shows AT MOST 5 top-level category rows plus the nsh sub-row, and rows are omitted entirely when structurally zero for that company (e.g. MCX/ETERNAL have no 'Promoters' row -- no promoter of record; RELIANCE/TCS/ITC/HDFCBANK have no 'Others' row). There is NO separate Mutual Funds row and NO separate Insurance row anywhere in the rendered table -- DII is one aggregate bucket, same DEF_DIFF shape as our old pre-Sep-2022 format (T2). Screener does NOT split FII into FPI-vs-FDI or break out banks/AIFs the way the new NSE XBRL format does; its categories read as OLD-FORMAT-style buckets (promoters/FII/DII/govt/public(+others)) applied uniformly across all eras with only a one-line footnote: "* The classifications might have changed from Sep'2022 onwards... Classifications such as banks and foreign portfolio investors were not available earlier." No mapping card work can assign MF/insurance until Phase 2 -- per T7, this site's DII must be diffed as one bucket against our fii+dii+mf+ins is wrong; likely correct comparison is screener DII ~= our dii+mf+ins (needs P2 mapping-card confirmation, not decided here).
depth_reliance: quarterly tab: Sep-2023 (earliest of a fixed 12-quarter/3-year rolling window, latest Jun-2026); yearly tab: Mar-2017 (one column per FY end, plus the latest quarter Jun-2026) -- so RELIANCE's earliest visible shareholding data point on screener.in is Mar-2017, 19 distinct quarters total once quarterly+yearly are merged (dedup on the 7 overlap-free years Mar-2017..Mar-2023).
depth_mcx: identical window shape: quarterly Sep-2023->Jun-2026 (12 qtrs), yearly Mar-2017->Jun-2026 (11 cols) -> 19 distinct quarters, earliest Mar-2017.
depth_eternal: quarterly Sep-2023->Jun-2026 (12 qtrs, same as others); yearly only Mar-2022->Jun-2026 (6 cols, IPO-bound -- Zomato listed Jul-2021, FY22 is its first full year) -> 14 distinct quarters, earliest Mar-2022.
depth_probe_pre2010_detail: All 4 probes (RELIANCE, TCS, ITC, HDFCBANK) show the IDENTICAL yearly-table floor 'Mar 2017' regardless of how long the company has been listed/covered (TCS listed 2004, ITC and RELIANCE far older, HDFCBANK 1995) -- this is a site-wide fixed display window (last ~10 FY + latest quarter), not a per-company data-availability limit. No quarter <= Jun-2010 is shown for ANY probe. That era (Dec-2002..Jun-2010, our 0%-covered era) is NOT recoverable from screener.in's anonymous view for any of the 4 probes. Whether a logged-in/premium account unlocks pre-2017 shareholding history is UNKNOWN -- not tested (no-login rule); screener's own premium marketing copy (/premium/) does not mention shareholding-pattern depth as a paid feature, unlike its financials tables which explicitly gate '+N more years', so this may simply be all the data screener holds rather than a paywall. Flag for orchestrator: if pre-2010 coverage is needed, screener is very unlikely to be the route regardless of login status.
event_rows_note: All emitted quarters are standard quarter-end/FY-end columns (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec); no mid-quarter/event-based columns were observed in either the quarterly or yearly tables for any of the 3 probes.
